MICROSOFT MAKES BOLDEST MOVE YET EMBRACING OPEN SOURCE -- In major turnaround, software giant 
promises "greater transparency" in its development and business practices, outlines a new strategy 
to provide more access to APIs and proprietary protocols, and acknowledges the significant impact 
open source and open standards have had on its business and the industry. Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/techwatch/archives/016011.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 
*Related blog: Microsoft opens APIs. Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/techwatch/archives/016011.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 
 
IS JAVA HEADED FOR RETIREMENT? -- At nearly 13, the app dev platform is looking old, compared 
with a new generation of scripting languages and frameworks. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/21/08NF-java-react_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 

IS COUNTING OPEN SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS USEFUL? -- The folks at startup Ohloh would give an 
emphatic "yes" nod, but its effort have raised the hackles of open source contributors. 
Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/tech-bottom-line/archives/2008/02/the_open_source.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 

CASHING IN ON GREEN IT -- For a mere $50,000 and three months implementation time, 
The Planet saved a cool $1 million in power this year. Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/sustainableit/archives/2008/02/green_planet_co.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 

DEPSITE YAHOO DRAMA, MICROSOFT FORGES AHEAD WITH SEARCH -- With the proposed acquisition 
that could disrupt its entire search strategy, Microsoft expands its enterprise and 
Internet search offerings with new FAST and Live Search products. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/20/Despite-Yahoo-drama-Microsoft-forges-ahead-with-search_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 

MCAFEE: VIRUS WRITERS ACTING LOCALLY -- No longer interested in worldwide attention, 
or law enforcement action, virus writes are focusing more regionally and ushering 
in the era of localized malware. Read on: 
http://www.infoworld.com/article/08/02/21/McAfee-Virus-writers-going-local_1.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
 

VISTA, EVEN WITH SP1, STILL SLOWER THAN XP -- Randall Kennedy issues a reminder 
that, when it comes to productivity applications, services, multimedia tasks, 
"Vista is an absolute dog compared to XP." Read on: 
http://weblog.infoworld.com/enterprisedesktop/archives/2008/02/news_flash_vist.html?source=NLC-DAILY&cgd=2008-02-21
